title: bioThreatFinder: two-stage metagenomic screening and in-silico confirmation of high-consequence pathogens
description:
A Nextflow pipeline for metagenomic screening and in-silico confirmation of high-consequence pathogens across human, animal and plant health. A permissive stage-1 screen across several classifier arms feeds a strict, per-candidate stage 2 that maps reads against each target together with its near neighbours, so reads that fit a harmless relative better are attributed to the relative rather than to the agent. A marker-gene tier gates the top evidence tier wherever the chromosome is not the actionable signal.

DISCLAIMER: research software, not a validated diagnostic assay. Sequence detection does not establish a viable organism, an active infection, or exposure. No threshold in packs/*/pack.yaml is a measured operating point; sensitivity and specificity are not characterised for any intended use; the watchlist is not an authoritative legal source for any jurisdiction; and the marker tier addresses gaps for which no published method exists, which is also why it is unvalidated. Coverage is incomplete and partly measured: 19 of 90 watchlist taxa are reachable through one stage-1 arm only, and 31 of 90 cannot reach the top evidence tier at all. No output of this software should be used to decide that a sample is safe. Any result bearing on a real decision requires confirmation by a validated, fit-for-purpose method. See DISCLAIMER.md.

The pipeline needs the databases deposited separately at doi:10.5281/zenodo.23602998 - the pinned NCBI taxonomy snapshot and the curated marker-gene database, which cannot be re-created from public sources. Everything else it needs is built by its own scripts, with every reference pinned by accession and by the checksum of its decompressed sequence.
